correctness.rationale: TARGET affirmative disintegration proof audited: center inclusion, Takesaki decomposition over Z(M)=Linf(Y), fiber identification as free ergodic amenable crossed products, global-to-local intertwining via Popa sequential criterion plus JvN selector with diagonal wn=u(n,n), fiberwise conjugacy via cited Popa factor criterion (Mn lemma for finite fibers), and Borel gluing of Gy via countable-generator tests. originality.rationale: Fused search over literal, equivalent, and dominance queries found only ergodic-factor Cartan theory: CFW81 automorphism conjugacy in R, Popa-Vaes unique-Cartan for nonamenable factors, Popa-Shlyakhtenko-Vaes regular-subalgebra automorphism classification. None states unitary conjugacy in a fixed non-ergodic non-factor amenable crossed product from full-central-support intertwining. Body-level inspections of CFW81 (automorphism, not unitary; ergodic R only), Popa-Shlyakhtenko-Vaes (automorphism classification of regular B in the factor R, not fiberwise unitary gluing under intertwining hypotheses in non-factors), Connes-Jones (non-conjugate Cartans in nonamenable factors, opposite direction), and Popa-Vaes (free-group factor unique Cartan, nonamenable ergodic) exclude coverage. No table, database, census, or stronger theorem subsumes the exact hypothesis.

value.rationale: TARGET result answers the admitted two-sided question affirmatively with a transferable reduction lemma (global full-support intertwining localizes to a.e. fiber via selector/diagonal argument) and a unitary-conjugacy rigidity theorem for Cartans in non-ergodic amenable group-measure-space algebras. This advances the recognized Cartan uniqueness program beyond ergodic factors to direct-integral gluing, is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration, and a future researcher can retrieve the exact invariant and lemma. Satisfies STANDARD eligible finding form (new theorem/structural lemma).

Ozawa-Popa, Ioana AFP, Speelman-Vaes: nonamenable unique/non-unique Cartan rigidity - metadata scope, disjoint hypotheses.
